title: Single sign-on
providersHint: Staff sign in with their company account. The first sign-in creates the person and their roles from the provider’s groups.
emptyHint: Connect a SAML 2.0 or OpenID Connect provider.
enforcementHint: Applies at the next sign-in. Existing sessions stay open. Emergency access uses password and fresh TOTP only.
require: Require single sign-on for all staff
breakGlassHint: Choose up to three active install admins with a password and enabled two-factor authentication.
spHint: Shared by every SAML connection on this install.
sync: How roles are kept in sync
syncHint: Each sign-in updates only this provider’s SSO roles. Roles an admin gave by hand are never changed.
name: Name
providerHint: Helpdock reads OIDC endpoints from issuer discovery. SAML values come from your identity provider.
label: Button label
allowIdpInitiated: Allow sign-in started from the identity provider
domainsHint: Comma-separated domains. New identity links require a verified email in these domains.
mfaHint: Enable only when your provider policy requires MFA for every sign-in. Helpdock then skips local TOTP.
mappingsHint: The first matching row for each brand wins. Reorder rows to change priority.
testHint: Sign in at the provider in a new window. The preview saves no accounts, identities, roles or sessions.
testEnabled: Save and enable the connection before testing it.
conflict: Another provider owns a matching brand role. Sign-in would be refused.
deleteHint: A connection linked to a staff identity cannot be deleted. Disable it instead.
error: Could not load single sign-on settings.
saveError: Could not save. Check the fields, permissions and emergency admin requirements.
invalid: Check the connection fields and mappings.
copyError: Copy failed. Select and copy the value.
popupBlocked: Allow pop-up windows to test this connection.
certificateHint: Paste a PEM signing certificate from your identity provider. Keep the current certificate during rotation.
invalidCertificate: The signing certificate is invalid. Use an RSA certificate with at least 2048 bits.

refusals.sso-email-domain-taken: {{domains}} already belongs to another enabled connection. Each email domain signs in through one enabled connection only.
refusals.sso-metadata-confirm-certificates: The provider metadata lists a signing certificate that is not saved here. Verify it with your identity provider, add it under Signing certificates, then save.

presets.label: Start from
presets.hint: A preset fills in the fields below. You can still change any of them.

google-workspace.name: Google Workspace (OIDC)
google-workspace.banner: Google Workspace: create the OAuth client in the Google Cloud project of your Workspace, with the consent screen set to Internal.
google-workspace.issuerHint: Google uses this one issuer for every Workspace.
google-workspace.groupsHint: Leave empty. Google sends no groups in the ID token, so use default access or give roles by hand.
google-workspace.domainsHint: Enter your Workspace domain, for example example.com. Only addresses there can link to this connection.

entra-id.name: Microsoft Entra ID (OIDC)
entra-id.banner: Microsoft Entra ID: register a single-tenant app with a Web redirect to this connection’s redirect URI. Under Token configuration, add the optional claims email, xms_edov and acct, and the groups claim.
entra-id.groupsHint: Add the groups claim in Token configuration. Values are group object IDs.
entra-id.domainsHint: Enter the verified domains of your Entra tenant, for example example.com.
